metadata.case_name: CHAN CHUN WA v. WONG CHIU YUEN ANDREW

injuries.description: whiplash injury of the cervical spine with residual pain and stiffness
source: it was their joint opinions that the Plaintiff suffered whiplash injury of the cervical spine with residual pain and stiffness, that the diagnosis was consistent with the mechanism of the injury as a result of the accident which caused the persistent symptoms claimed.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

source: sprained neck and right elbow contusion
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine

source: sprained neck and right elbow contusion

injuries.description: soft tissue injury on his neck
source: he was told he suffered from soft tissue injury on his neck.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of muscle, fascia or tendon at neck level

manifestations.description: mild tenderness over the posterior neck with reduced range of neck motion
muscle spasm over the right side of his neck
mild pain over his right elbow
numbness along elbow and down to ulnar side of hand and wrist (subsided)
limitation of motions of the cervical region especially in lateral rotation
residual pain and stiffness over his neck region

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Plaintiff claimed he used to enjoy playing football and swimming prior to the accident. He claimed he could no longer play football or swim due to the neck pain.
Dr. Kong commented that Mr. Chan may find difficulty to maintain a job as a driver because of the neck pain on rotation.
